# Pixtega

> On-demand image derivation service, written in Rust. It fetches an image from an operator-configured source (HTTP(S), filesystem, or S3), derives a bounded variant (width, format, optional quality), and returns cacheable image bytes. One Rust binary or a Lambda container image; TOML config; MIT licensed.

The entire HTTP API is one GET endpoint:
`GET {base}{pathPrefix}/{mount}/{source-path}/w{width}[,q{quality}].{format}[?v=token]`.
The default `pathPrefix` is `/images`. `format` is one of `webp`, `avif`, `jpeg` (no aliases). `{mount}` selects an operator-configured source — callers never pass a hostname, bucket, or directory. Width and quality must be in server-configured allowlists; omitting `q` uses the format's default, and spelling out the default is rejected so each derived image has exactly one URL. `v` is an opaque cache-busting token only; it is never sent upstream, and the `version_token` config key can ignore or reject it. The service never upscales.

The JavaScript client is pure URL builders for this contract: `pixtegaUrl`, `pixtegaSrcSet`, `pixtegaPicture`. It builds strings and never fetches.

Full documentation as one Markdown file: https://pixtega.com/llms-full.txt

## Docs

- [Home](https://pixtega.com/): what Pixtega is and why — one original, allowlisted sizes, CDN-friendly caching
- [Getting started](https://pixtega.com/docs/getting-started.html): quick start with bundled fixtures, build dependencies (libvips), Docker
- [Configuration](https://pixtega.com/docs/configuration.html): TOML schema, config precedence, limits and ranges, source transports, S3 credentials
- [API reference](https://pixtega.com/docs/api.html): URL grammar, caching table, error taxonomy, response headers, observability
- [AWS Lambda](https://pixtega.com/docs/aws-lambda.html): Lambda container image with the Web Adapter, deployment outline, production exposure

## Code and packages

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/kroofy/Pixtega): source, issues, releases
- [README](https://github.com/kroofy/Pixtega/blob/main/README.md): the reference for service behavior and operation
- [pixtega on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/pixtega): the Rust crate and binary
- [pixtega on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/pixtega): JavaScript URL builders for the service's URL contract
- [@pixtega/url on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pixtega/url): thin re-export of the `pixtega` npm package, same API
